sara (perf): FYI saw a ~12% 99th-tail latency regression after the INT8 rollout on gpt-smallish when prefix KV caching is enabled. Profiling points to extra memcpy + a fallback matmul on layer 8.

mike (runtime): Can you paste the perf snippet and which infra (dedicated vs hosted) this hit on?

sara (perf): Hosted canary (us-west-2, dedicated pool). Quick log extract: 
```
[perf] model=gpt-smallish seq=1024 bs=1 prefix_cached=true
selected_kernel=quant_int8_mha_fast (attempt)
layer=8 kernel_fallback=fp32_mha_slow reason=scale_overflow
kv_restore bytes=512k time=2.3ms memcpy=1.8ms
overall token_ms=18.7 (was 16.7 baseline)
```
Looks like the selector decided int8 for most layers but flipped to fp32 at runtime for layer 8 causing two things: extra KV restore roundtrip + incompat write into cache.

dinesh (infra): Hmm, recent kernel-selector tweak (rev: 3f4a7b2) changed the overflow threshold and the path that handles mixed-precision KV writes. Could be a calibration delta. Reproducer command to run locally: 
```bash
./run_inference --model gpt-smallish --seq 1024 --prefix-cache on --quant-mode int8 --profile kernels
```
Run that on a GPU with cuBLAS deterministic off.

anya (ml): I ran a calibration sweep last week and layer 8 shows high activation variance for our int8 scale method. Per-layer sensitivity: 
- layers 0-6: safe int8
- layer 7: borderline
- layer 8: sensitive (drops ppl by ~1.3)
- final layers+lm_head: exclude from quantization.
My calibration artifact: https://artifacts.internal/ci/calib/2026-02-11 (contains maps + per-layer stats).

mike (runtime): Two quick mitigations: (1) runtime flag to force fp32 for a layer mask (cheap), (2) fallback to storing KV in fp32 when layer flips to fp32 to avoid re-encoding on read. Option (2) needs careful memory accounting.

sara (perf): I tried forcing fp32 for layers 6-9 and tail latency returns to baseline. But unit cost increases ~6%. Tradeoff seems acceptable until we get better INT8 kernel.

dinesh (infra): Agree. I'll open a canary rollback for the kernel-selector commit and add a hotfix that: 
- honors --quant-exclude=embeddings,lm_head by default for now, and
- exposes --runtime-mixed-mask to pin layers to fp32 on the worker side.
Ticket: INF-2387 created.

anya (ml): For the longer term we should add per-layer calibration in the model onboarding pipeline and emit a sensitivity map that the runtime can consume at launch. Example pseudocode to apply per-layer scale/skip: 
```python
for layer_idx, layer in enumerate(model.layers):
    if sensitivity_map[layer_idx] > THRESHOLD:
        layer.quant_mode = 'fp32'  # runtime honor
    else:
        layer.quant_mode = 'int8'
```
We also need a deterministic test that exercises KV cache + mixed precision transitions.

mike (runtime): Can someone drop a small repro script into the ticket? If we have CI microbench that toggles kv cache + layer mask we can gate the rollback.

sara (perf): Dropping a tiny repro here (paste in ticket): 
```python
# repro.py - iterate prefix lengths to hit restore path
from runner import Client
c = Client(model='gpt-smallish', quant='int8', prefix_cache=True)
for p in [0,64,256,512,1024]:
    out=c.generate(prefix_len=p, seq_len=1024)
```
This reliably reproduces the memcpy spike on the canary node.

infra-bot: [alert] metric(redwood.hosted.us-west2.gpt-smallish.tail_99) crossed threshold 12% above baseline at 1768204321 :rotating_light:

mike (runtime): OK assigning tasks:

- anya: generate a per-layer sensitivity export for the model catalog (ML-487)

I'll run a microbench in staging once the hotfix is up.
